FOR E ,V 0 R 0

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 7 December 1967, after the draft finalized by the Timber Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council.
0.2 As timber is extensively used for various purposes in mining, such as pit props, bars, cogging sleepers, tram sleepers, bantam and ladders, a need is felt to have a standard for use of timber in the coal mining in the first instance.

0.3 The prevailing conditions in mines are generally humid and hot. Some mines are very wet, especially the coal winning places where hydraulic sand stowing is practised. Indian coals are liable to spontaneous heating which subsequently may cause fire in the coal. Besides, some mines are gassy which may cause explosion and subsequent fire. Thus to reduce the spread of any fire, the timbers used in the mines shall also be treated for fire resistance unless it is otherwise considered safe by the users.

0.4 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-odination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in iIiis country.
O.S This standard contains clause 4.2.6 which permits the purchaser to use his option {pr selection to suit his requirements. 0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with. the final values, observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2..1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off values should be the same as that of the specified values in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements of timber with regard to species, sizes and their treatment when used in coal mines. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions and those given in IS : 707-1958* shall apply. 2.1 Bantam - A piece of timber of about IS X 20 em in cross-section and about four metres in length (see Fig. 1 ) used for supporting power cables, pipes, etc.

4.2.6 Timber of any other sizes and for any other purposes may also be supplied as required by the users.

4.3 MelsaremeDts 4.3.1 Length of the members shall be measured between the extreme ends correct to one centimetre. 4.3.2 The cross-section dimension (diametre, breadth, width) shall be measured at the centre portion of the length of the member correct to 2 mm,

s, DEFECfS
5.1 Defeets Totally Prohibited - The following defects in the timber for use in mines shall be totally prohibited: a) b) c) d) Sap rot, Hollows in the top of a prop, Cross breaks, and Large holes.

5.2 Defects Permitted to a Limited Extent 5.2.1 Dead Streaks - Timber for use in mines shall be free from
dead streaks that are wider than the one-fourth of the circumference of the timber at the point of measurement.

5.2.2 Decay - Timber for use in mines shall be free from decay and visible evidence of the presence of wood rotting fungi. 5.2.3 Checks and Splits - Timbers for use in mines shall not have in the end surface splits or checks extending from one point of the periphery to another point or more than one-tenth of the length along the surface. 5.2.4 Hollow Heart - No timber for use in mines shall have hollow heart, the diameter of which exceeds one-fourth the end diameter or the depth of which exceeds one-tenth of the length. The depth of hollow heart shall be measured from the end surface. ..
S.2.5 Rot - Rot in pith may be permitted in the end surface provided the aggregate of rot and hollow heart does not exceed 25 percent of the entire end surfaces.

5.16 Ring Shake - Complete ring shakes on the end surface may be permitted provided the diameter of the ting which they follow is not more than one-third of the diameter at the end, and provided the depth is not more than one-tenth of the length.
8

IS : 4424 - 1M7

5.'1,.7 Insee: Damage - Timber for use in mines shall be free from insect damage except that total number of pin holes to the extent of 10 in every 1000 eml may be permitted and the concentration ofsueh holes shall be not greater than 10 in any 2S em'.
5.2.8 Knols 5.2.8.1 Unsound knots - Timber for use in mines shall be free from unsound knots over 20 mm in diameter. 5.2.8.2 Sound knots - The diameter of any single sound knot or
the sum of the diameters of all sound knots in any section, 30 em in length, between the two ends of the props, bars, cogging, sleepers, tram sleepers and bantam shall not exceed the following: a) Maximum diameter of any single sound knot 75 mm, and b) Sum of maximum diameters of all sound knots 200 mm.
N OTlD - Knots of diameter 10 rom and under shall be ignored in applying the limitations for the Bum of diameters. The sum of maxi. mum diameters of all sound knots acroSB any section of the timber for USB in mines shall not esceed 25 peroent of ciroumCerence at that seotion.

6. PRESERVATIVES

6.1 The treatments to be given shall conform to IS: 401-1967*.
7. DESIGN 7.1 Props shall be designed as a strut column as given in IS: 883-1966t.
7.2 Bars shall be designed as a beam supported at two ends with uniformly distributed load or several point.. loads.

7.3 Cogging .e1eepers shall be designed for areas under compresslon as per IS : 883-1966t. 7.4 Tram sleepers shall be designed as under 7.3. 7.5 Bantam shall be designed as a beam under several point-loading. 8. MARKING 8.1 Each timber shall be marked in a suitable manner with the manufacturer's identification mark or initials.

NOTB - The use of the lSI Certitlcation Mark is governed by the provision. of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certifioation Marks) Aot, and the BuIes and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on produots covered by an Indian Standard oonveys the assurance that they have been produced to oomply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-def ned system of inspeotion, testing and quality oontrol during produotion. This system, whioh is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as aotually marketed are oontinuously cheeked by lSI for oonformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under whioh a licence for the use of the lSI Certifioation Hark may be granted to manufaoturers or processors, may be obtain� ed from the Indian Standards Institution.

INDIAN STANDARDS INSTITUTION
The Indian Standards Institution ( 151 ). which stareed functlon'n. In 1947. Is the national standards organization for Indta. Its principal object Is to prepare standards on national and International basla and promote their leneral adoption.
The overall control of 151. which II run and financed Jointly I I � non-profit making body by the Government and private enterprise, Is exercised by the General Council. composed of representatives of Central and State Governments; leading trade, scientific and technological organizations; and subscribing members. The Union Minister of Industry Is the ex-offlclo President of 151.

The present technical activity of lSI Is carried out through 8 Division Councils for Agricultural and Food Products; Chemical; Civil Engineering; Consumer Products; Electrotechnlcal; Mechanical Engineering; Structural and Metals; and Textile. All technical work relating co the formulation and revision of standards Is done by committees appointed by and under the direction of their respectivi Division Councils. These committees consist of experts drawn from manufacturlnl units, technical Institutions. purchase orcanlzatlonl and other concerned bodies.
To make Ivallable benefits of Indian Standards to che common min, lSI hal Introduced Its Certification Marks Scheme under the IndIan Scandard. Institution (Certl~cGtlon Marks) Act, 1952, as amended by the Amendment Ace, 1961. According to this Act. quality goods conforming to IndianStandards can carry the 151 Certlflcatlon Mark. This Mark Is � thlrd-part1luarantee of quality of marked goods. Licence. to use the 151 Certification Mark are cranted to manufacturers using

reliable methods of quail ty control sublect to overall Inspection by 151.
In the International fteld, IS' represencs India on the Internitlonal Oraanlzatlon for Standardization ( ISO) and the In~ernatlonal Electrotechnical Commission ( lEe ). ISO and lEe respectively link S4 and 40 countries. and function throu.h 118 and 58 technical committees; 151 participates In 83 technical committees of ISO and all the technical commltt��� of lEe. The committees and subcommittees of lEe and ISO for which 151 holds the secretariat deal With: Electric Fans, LIC, Mica, Pictorial Markin,s for Handling of Goods, Liquid Flow Measur.� ments In Open Channels, Procedures for Inter-conversion of Values.
